distractors.reason: 'Good' is an adjective. We use it before a noun (a good night), not after the verb. We don't say 'sleep good'.
'Fast' describes speed of movement. We don't say 'sleep fast' to mean sleeping well.
'Loudly' describes sound. It does not describe the quality of sleep, so 'sleep loudly' is not a standard collocation.

l1_interference: Türkçede zarf genellikle fiilden önce gelir ('iyi uyumak' yapısında olduğu gibi). Bu yüzden öğrenciler 'good sleep' veya 'sleep good' gibi yanlış sıralamalar yapabilir. İngilizcede 'well' zarfı fiilden sonra gelir: 'sleep well'. Ayrıca 'iyi' anlamındaki 'good' sıfatı fiilden sonra kullanılmaz.
explanation: 'Well' is an adverb that tells how an action is done. It usually comes after the verb: sleep well, listen carefully, work hard.

related_collocations.example: Please listen carefully to the teacher.
I work hard every morning before school.
My grandfather eats slowly at dinner.

memory_tip: WELL = how well an action is done (sleep well, eat well) | GOOD = describes a noun (a good night)
